clue.text: Typical end — a race to keep list of appointments

indicators.note: the run of clue words holds the letters within it, as a box might keep something stored inside

explanation.surface: Someone sighs that a race is the usual way to finish off a busy schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across typiCAL END A Race, ignoring the dash; 'to keep' signals that the words hold the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A diary or planner of dated engagements is a common sense of the word, as in a busy social one.

clue.text: Attack fee

definitions.meaning: a rush forward at an enemy, as cavalry might make
a price asked for a service

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions side by side: a military rush and a price.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a headlong assault and a sum demanded for goods or services.

clue.text: Fish rising means flexibility

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word rising is read from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: an eel is a snakelike fish
a way is a method or means of doing something

explanation.surface: A fish swimming upward is evidence of a supple, adaptable creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Room to manoeuvre or tolerance for deviation, originally the drift of a ship to downwind.

clue.text: Elevated part of heel-bone is impressive

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted up means the letters are read upwards, from the bottom
only a section of the hyphenated word is taken

explanation.surface: A raised section of the heel bone looks remarkable on an X-ray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' takes ELBON from heEL-BONe and 'Elevated' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand or stately in appearance, as in a fine building of imposing proportions.

clue.text: Like tense journey on a horse?

parts.note: as means in the manner of, like
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a ride is a trip or journey

explanation.surface: A nervous trip in the saddle, posed as a question about what horse riding feels like.
explanation.definitionFit: With legs either side, the usual posture of a rider in the saddle; the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: Speaks of total chaos at the back

parts.note: utter means complete or total, as in utter nonsense

indicators.note: the letter at the back of the word chaos is its last one

explanation.surface: Someone describes complete disorder at the rear of a room.
explanation.definitionFit: To say or voice words aloud is a plain synonym for talking.

clue.text: Go after extra shifts, getting financial statement

indicators.note: after places the go piece behind the rearranged letters
the letters of the word extra are shifted about into a new order

parts.note: a turn is a go, as in a game

explanation.surface: Taking on overtime shifts means a more complicated report for the tax office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' rearranges EXTRA to TAXRE; TURN comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A form declaring income to the revenue authorities is a statement of one's finances.

clue.text: Take strength from tea? Never settled!

indicators.note: the letters are settled into a different arrangement, as a dispute might be resolved

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether tea saps energy, then insists the matter was never decided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settled' rearranges the letters of TEA and NEVER together.
explanation.definitionFit: To weaken or drain someone of vigour; a verb phrase matching the verb.

clue.text: Reserve group comment on stage

parts.note: a set is a group of things or people
an aside is a remark an actor makes to the audience, unheard by the other characters

explanation.surface: A theatre group's backstage comment about holding something in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something by for later use or keep it in reserve, as a verb.

clue.text: Bitterness of a tribe lost in deserted city

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
the word city deserted by its insides leaves just its outer letters
the letters of tribe are lost, that is jumbled up and disordered

explanation.surface: A people who lost their way in an empty city became sour about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserted' empties CITY to CY; 'lost' rearranges TRIBE to ERBIT, which goes inside, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpness or sourness of taste or temper is a direct synonym for bitterness.

clue.text: Reckon missing Conservative will be replaced by Republican authority

indicators.note: the conservative letter goes missing from the word for reckon
the gap left is filled by the republican letter instead

parts.note: to expect is to reckon or suppose
C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the UK party
R is the abbreviation for Republican, the US party

explanation.surface: A political pundit predicts a Tory being swapped out for a Republican specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of specialist knowledge, an authority on a subject, is the same thing as a specialist.

clue.text: Engage in some shenanigans

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A command to join in with some mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across soME SHenanigans.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears engage when their teeth interlock, which is the verb's sense here.

clue.text: Source of information about origin of wine?

definitions.text: Source of information about origin of wine?

parts.words: Source of information about origin of wine?
parts.note: wine comes from the plant bearing grapes, and the phrase 'heard it through' this plant means learned by rumour

explanation.walkthrough: The plant that wine originates on is also the informal network by which gossip spreads.
explanation.definitionFit: An unofficial chain of rumour is the idiomatic sense; the literal sense is the climbing plant fruit grows on.

clue.text: Singer is following the Spanish victory

indicators.note: following places the word is after the other pieces

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
V is short for victory, as in a V-sign

explanation.surface: A singer follows up a Spanish triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: Presley, the rock and roll star, is an example of a vocalist.

clue.text: Man perhaps American ejected from passage

indicators.note: the American letter is thrown out of the passage word

parts.note: an aisle is a passage between rows of seats

explanation.surface: An American is thrown out of a passageway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person here: the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Man is an example of a small island, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Pat's mug?

parts.note: a pat is a gentle tap of the hand, and a mug is a gullible person easily talked into giving money

explanation.walkthrough: Looks like a person called Pat and their cup or face; read instead as a gentle stroke and an easy victim.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle stroke is literally this, and the idiom means a person easily persuaded to hand over money.

clue.text: Searched around area, tormented

indicators.note: the searching word goes around the area letter

parts.note: hunted means searched for

explanation.surface: Someone who scoured the neighbourhood ended up in agony.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubled or obsessed by a persistent memory or fear, as a ghost plagues a house.

clue.text: Turn on pretence that is about duty

parts.note: an act is a pretence, as in putting on an act

indicators.note: the that-is letters wrap about the duty

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for that is (id est)
VAT, value added tax, is a UK duty on goods

explanation.surface: Someone switches on the charm as a pretext for discussing tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To start a device or set it working is to switch it on.

clue.text: More flexible about one's provider

indicators.note: the more-flexible word goes about the letter for one

parts.note: suppler is the comparative of supple, bending easily
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A vendor who is more accommodating than one's usual source.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm or person furnishing goods or services is a provider.

clue.text: Mallard may have done this if very happy

definitions.meaning: Mallard is a famous British steam locomotive, which would puff along making a chugging noise
British slang for delighted or pleased

explanation.walkthrough: Mallard looks like a duck, but it is the record-breaking steam engine; steam engines puff as they move.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam train's puffing noise is one sense; British slang for thoroughly pleased is the other.

clue.text: Fruit that has a sell-by, for example

definitions.meaning: a sweet brown fruit of a palm tree
a sell-by is one example of a day printed on food packaging

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: a palm fruit, and the kind of day a sell-by marks.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm fruit shares its name with a calendar day, of which a sell-by is one example.

clue.text: Grass may be evil — and good

parts.note: a sin is something that may be evil, a wicked act

explanation.surface: Lawn grass might be wicked, and virtuous too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' here is British slang for informing on someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are underworld slang for betraying accomplices to the police, as a verb.

clue.text: Leave out exercise runs for captain

parts.note: to skip is to omit or leave out
PE is physical education, school exercise
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A team leader skips exercise sessions and running.
explanation.definitionFit: The master of a ship or leader of a sports team is informally called this.

clue.text: Son's mounting trouble providing line

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means climbing upward, so read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
if means providing, on condition that

explanation.surface: A son faces growing difficulties if he follows the family line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns AIL and IF upwards into FILIA. 'Son's' is a possessive standing for an adjective, which is fair: a son's duty is a filial duty.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes what belongs to or befits a son or daughter, as in duty.

clue.text: Said yes to a vice?

parts.note: greed is one of the deadly sins, a vice

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether consenting meant giving in to a moral failing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gave consent or assented to something; a past-tense verb phrase.

clue.text: Popular place making contribution

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to put is to place

explanation.surface: A trendy venue that adds its share to a project.
explanation.definitionFit: A share offered to a discussion or project, such as ideas or effort, is a contribution.

clue.text: Instant suspicion by these wives, initially

indicators.note: by means next to, so the initials stand beside the suspicion word
taking the initial letter of each of the two words that come before it

parts.note: an inkling is a faint suspicion or hint

explanation.surface: A sudden doubt about these particular wives.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'in the blink of an eye' has a twin meaning a very brief moment, an instant.

clue.text: Succeeded after enthusiastic cries

indicators.note: after places the succeeded letter at the end

parts.note: keen means eager or enthusiastic
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone triumphed after loud, eager shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cries' is a verb here: to wail in grief, as at an Irish funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To wail in mourning for the dead is a sense of crying out loud.

clue.text: Target incorporating North American hatred

indicators.note: the target word takes the north letter into its body

parts.note: an aim is a target or goal
US means American

explanation.surface: A target that takes in North America is a sign of enmity.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility or ill will toward someone; the Latin word for mind has come to mean animosity.

clue.text: A head of publicity with very little desire

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: petite means small and dainty

explanation.surface: A publicity chief who wants very little.
explanation.definitionFit: A craving or hunger for food, or a wish for anything, is a desire.

clue.text: He's upset about skill and makes connection to ground

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about the skill word
the letters of he's are upset, knocked into a different order

parts.note: art is a skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A man is distressed about the craft of connecting wires to the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges HES to EHS, and 'about' puts it round ART.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrician grounds a circuit by wiring it to the soil, which British English calls this verb.

clue.text: Fought women, relaxed about right of appeal

indicators.note: the relaxed word goes about the letter from appeal

parts.note: rested means relaxed

indicators.note: the rightmost letter of the word appeal, its last

explanation.surface: Women who were calm grappled over a legal right to appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right of appeal' looks like a legal phrase, but it is the far-right letter, L, of 'appeal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappled hand to hand, or struggled with a problem; a past-tense verb meaning combated.
